content.title: About
content.content: Potato salad with creamy dressing is a classic dish made from boiled potatoes, eggs, vegetables and a rich creamy dressing based on mayonnaise, sour cream or yogurt. It is popular as a side dish or snack at picnics, parties and family meals.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first recorded potato salad recipe appeared in the United States in the early 1920s.
Different countries add unique ingredients: Germany often includes apples, Japan uses seaweed.
A yogurt‑based dressing can make the salad lower in calories while keeping it creamy.
Although usually served cold, some recipes call for a brief warm‑up before serving.
The traditional Russian version frequently contains pickles and green onions.

items.title: Source of potassium
items.content: Potatoes are rich in potassium, which helps maintain normal blood pressure and muscle function.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: The salad provides vitamin B6 and folate, important for metabolism and nervous system health.

items.title: Protein from eggs
items.content: Eggs add complete protein that supports tissue repair and satiety.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: When vegetables and herbs are included, the fiber content improves digestion.

items.title: Healthy fats
items.content: Using yogurt or a light mayo reduces saturated fat while keeping the dish satisfying.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: Traditional mayo‑based versions are calorie‑dense, so portion control is advisable.

items.title: Egg allergy
items.content: People allergic to eggs should use egg‑free proteins or alternative dressings.

items.title: Bacterial growth risk
items.content: If left at room temperature for more than 2 hours, especially with mayo, the salad can become a breeding ground for bacteria.

items.title: Sodium level
items.content: Adding salty ingredients such as pickles or soy sauce can increase the sodium content.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the salad chilled, often alongside grilled meats, barbecue, or fish. Garnish with fresh herbs, radish slices or olives. For a lighter version, use a yogurt dressing and add extra fresh vegetables.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the prepared salad in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. Let it sit briefly before serving so the dressing fully penetrates the potatoes. Discard if it develops an off smell or color.
